tasks.short: Log call and mail outcomes, promises to pay and disputes in the AFAS debtor file.

today.trigger: After each debtor call, mail or reply, and at the weekly ageing review.
steps: Open the debtor in AFAS Profit and read the last notes
Type a summary of the call or mail into the debtor note
Update the Excel tracker with promise-to-pay date, amount and dispute flag
Forward dispute details to sales or operations in Outlook or Teams
Re-check the tracker on the promised date
drudgery: Retyping the same facts in AFAS and in Excel
Writing notes from memory after a run of calls
Chasing which promises fell due today
today.time_sinks: Double entry in AFAS and the Excel tracker, and notes that are too thin to use a month later.

lenses.faster: A model turns the call notes or mail thread into a structured note with promise date, amount, dispute reason and next step; the officer checks it in under a minute and the Excel tracker goes away.
lenses.autonomous: Every logged call or incoming debtor mail creates a draft note in AFAS; promises to pay become dated follow-up tasks; the officer approves notes only when a dispute or plan is involved.
lenses.ambitious: Dispute reasons recorded the same way on every invoice let Finance give sales and operations a monthly report on why shippers do not pay (damage, surcharges, missing POD). That is a new service, and demand for it grows as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping notes into two places; the officer wants more time on the conversations that resolve disputes.
lenses.options: Little value in multiple drafts; one accurate note is the goal.
lenses.altitude: The officer stops being a note-taker and owns the dispute-reason codes and follow-up rules that the whole order-to-cash process uses.
reach: Bookkeeper (AR): keep debtor master data and notes consistent
FP&A Analyst: feed promise-to-pay dates into the cash-in forecast

tasks.human_edge: Reading tone and intent in a conversation, telling a soft promise from a firm one, and keeping personal remarks out of the file.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns free text from calls and mails into fixed fields inside an existing AFAS workflow, and the output is easy to check.

in_practice.trigger: A call is logged or a debtor mail arrives in the shared collections mailbox.
steps: Pull the mail thread or the officer's quick call notes
Model extracts promise date, amount, dispute reason code and next action
Write a draft note and follow-up task to the AFAS debtor
Officer confirms notes that contain disputes or payment plans
in_practice.human_gate: The officer approves any note that records a dispute, a payment plan or an extension; plain status notes post directly.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS Profit debtor notes and tasks, with the source mail linked.

evidence.claim: 30% of Dutch finance and credit professionals name manual work in Excel, mail and exports as their biggest cash-flow problem.
Language models reliably extract structured fields such as dates and amounts from short business mails.

risks: Wrong promise date extracted, so follow-up fires on the wrong day
Personal data about sole-trader debtors kept longer than AVG allows
Model-written notes sound more certain than the conversation was
research_questions: Can AFAS Profit accept debtor notes and tasks through its connector API from an external workflow?
What share of collection notes today contain a usable dispute reason?
Does the works council need to be consulted if Teams call transcripts are used as input?

tasks.short: Run the AFAS ageing list each morning and decide which overdue shippers to chase first.

today.trigger: Every morning and before the weekly cash meeting with the Controller.
steps: Export the open-items ageing list from AFAS to Excel
Sort by days overdue and amount, and mark big or risky shippers
Check Power BI and notes for disputes and promises already made
Look up worrying debtors in the KvK register
Build the day's call and mail list
drudgery: Daily export and re-sorting in Excel
Cross-checking which items already have a promise or dispute
Manual KvK lookups
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding the same priority list by hand every day from a nightly extract.

lenses.faster: A scheduled report ranks open items by amount, days overdue, payment history and open disputes, and flags KvK changes; the officer spends ten minutes reviewing the list instead of an hour building it.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS refresh triggers the ranking and a KvK change check; the officer only handles flagged accounts such as an insolvency notice or a credit limit breach.
lenses.ambitious: A credit check before each new transport order rather than once a year: a decision made far more often, and demand for it grows as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the morning export ritual; the officer wants more time on the accounts that actually move DSO.
lenses.options: Two or three ranking rules (amount first, risk first, oldest first) side by side show which list cuts DSO most, and that changes the policy.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from list-making to setting credit limits and priority rules with the Controller, a more expert job with real decision rights on order blocks.
reach: Controller: propose credit limits and order-block rules
FP&A Analyst: weekly cash-in outlook from the ranked list

tasks.human_edge: Knowing that a big shipper always pays late but pays, or that a small haulier is in trouble before the data shows it.
tasks.pattern_why: Ranking and monitoring rules can be written down and run on the AFAS extract without a model.

steps: Pull open items, payment history and dispute flags from AFAS
Score each debtor with written rules (amount, days overdue, history, disputes)
Check KvK for changes such as insolvency or deregistration
Publish the ranked list in Power BI and flag exceptions to the officer
in_practice.human_gate: The officer approves any order block or credit limit change the list suggests.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI dataset with each day's list kept for audit; decisions noted in AFAS.

evidence.claim: 81% of 336 Dutch finance and credit professionals explain DSO after the fact rather than steering it.
Creditworthiness scoring of natural persons is high-risk under AI Act Annex III 5(b).
Annex III duties apply from 2 December 2027.

risks: A learned score on sole-trader hauliers would fall under AI Act high-risk duties; keep rules explicit
Nightly extract lag hides payments made today
Rules tuned on one season misrank in peak season
research_questions: How many debtors are sole traders or partnerships, and so natural persons under the AI Act?
Which KvK data product gives change alerts at a cost that fits?
Would a risk-first ranking have lowered DSO on last year's data?

tasks.short: Send reminders and call shippers whose invoices are overdue.

today.trigger: Invoices passing due date and the daily priority list.
steps: Pick overdue invoices from the ageing list
Run AFAS reminder letters or write mails in Outlook
Adjust wording by hand for key accounts
Phone debtors at the top of the list
Note outcomes in AFAS
drudgery: Hand-editing standard reminder text
Calculating interest and the EUR 40 compensation per invoice
Finding the right contact at the shipper
today.time_sinks: Writing reminder mails one by one and finding the right person to call.

lenses.faster: AFAS dunning runs a fixed sequence with interest and costs calculated by rule, and a model drafts the tone for key accounts; the officer reviews non-standard mails and makes the calls.
lenses.autonomous: Due date plus a set number of days triggers each reminder step; standard reminders go out without a person, while second notices for key accounts wait for approval.
lenses.ambitious: A polite check a week before due date for every shipper (invoice received, any questions?) is a new service to customers that cuts disputes, and use grows as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses hand-editing reminder letters; the officer wants more time on the calls that matter.
lenses.options: Two wordings for a second notice (firm versus relationship-first) let the officer pick the tone for a key account, which can decide whether the shipper pays or escalates.
lenses.altitude: The officer designs the reminder sequence and tone rules per customer segment instead of sending letters.
reach: Sales account managers: first contact on overdue key accounts

tasks.human_edge: Calling, listening and judging when to hold back a reminder because of a dispute or an ongoing sales conversation.
tasks.pattern_why: Sequence, timing, interest and costs are rules; a model only adjusts wording for a few accounts.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice reaches a set number of days past due.
steps: AFAS selects items for the next reminder step, skipping disputed ones
Rules calculate statutory commercial interest and the EUR 40 compensation
Model drafts tailored wording for key or sensitive accounts
Standard reminders send; tailored ones wait for the officer
in_practice.human_gate: The officer approves every non-standard reminder and every final notice before it goes.

evidence.claim: B2B statutory commercial interest runs from the agreed due date (or 30 days after invoice), and at least EUR 40 compensation is due without a reminder.
Errors in the first reminder, interest or costs surface only later in court.

risks: Reminder sent on a disputed invoice angers a key shipper
Wrong interest or cost calculation weakens a later court claim
Mail to an outdated contact goes unread
research_questions: Does AFAS dunning skip items flagged as disputed out of the box?
Are the payment terms agreed in each shipper contract recorded in AFAS?
Do tailored reminders get paid faster than standard ones on our own data?

tasks.short: Answer shippers' questions about their account: statements, invoice copies, proof of delivery.

today.trigger: Mails and calls from debtors asking about invoices or balances.
steps: Read the question in the shared mailbox
Look up the invoice and payments in AFAS
Ask operations for the proof of delivery or rate agreement
Write and send the answer with attachments
Note the question in AFAS
drudgery: Pulling statements and invoice copies by hand
Chasing operations for delivery proof
Answering the same balance question again
today.time_sinks: Waiting for operations to send proof of delivery or surcharge details.

lenses.faster: An agent reads the mail, pulls the statement, invoice copy and delivery proof, and drafts the reply; the officer approves in a minute instead of spending fifteen.
lenses.autonomous: Each incoming mail is classified; simple requests get a drafted reply with attachments, and disputes go to the officer as a case with the file assembled.
lenses.ambitious: Same-day answers for smaller shippers who now wait days, a group served properly for the first time, which shortens their time to payment.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses digging up invoice copies; the officer wants more time on real disputes.
lenses.options: Limited; one correct reply is the aim.
lenses.altitude: The officer handles disputes and decides which request types may later go out without review.
reach: Operations customer service: delivery proof requests

tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a simple question hides a dispute or complaint that should go to sales or operations.
tasks.pattern_why: Requests vary and the agent must decide which documents to fetch; a person approves before anything is sent.

in_practice.trigger: A mail lands in the collections mailbox.
steps: Classify the request (statement, copy, delivery proof, dispute)
Fetch open items and documents from AFAS and SharePoint
Draft the reply with attachments
Route disputes to the officer with the file assembled
in_practice.human_gate: The officer approves each reply before it is sent.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS debtor notes with the sent mail attached.

evidence.claim: Receivables suites claim up to 30% faster dispute handling, as indicative estimates with people on validation.

risks: Wrong attachment sent to another customer, an AVG and confidentiality breach
Delivery proof not stored where the agent can find it
Agent treats a dispute as a simple question
research_questions: Where are proofs of delivery stored today, and can they be found by invoice number?
What share of incoming mails are simple statement or copy requests?
How often would a drafted reply need correction in a two-week trial?

tasks.short: Talk shippers into paying, settle disputes and agree payment plans or extensions.

today.trigger: Accounts at the top of the overdue list or a debtor raising a dispute.
steps: Read the debtor history and open disputes in AFAS and mail
Gather delivery proof, damage claims or surcharge details
Call the debtor and negotiate
Agree a payment plan or extension and get approval
Confirm in writing and record it
drudgery: Building the dispute file from scattered mails
Writing confirmation mails after each call
today.time_sinks: Preparing for each conversation by gathering the full story.

lenses.faster: A copilot prepares a one-page brief per debtor (history, disputes, documents, past promises) and drafts the confirmation mail; the conversation itself takes as long as before.
lenses.autonomous: Briefs are built automatically for the day's call list; the officer leads every conversation and approves every plan.
lenses.ambitious: Structured payment-plan offers for small hauliers and shippers that now go straight to escalation or write-off, a group served for the first time.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses assembling the dispute file; the officer wants more of the negotiation itself.
lenses.options: Two or three payment-plan scenarios with cash effect and risk let the officer and Controller pick the plan, which changes the decision itself.
lenses.altitude: The officer becomes the negotiator with authority to approve plans and small settlements within set limits.
reach: Sales account managers: settling commercial disputes on surcharges
Controller: approving small write-offs within limits

tasks.human_edge: Persuasion, empathy and judgement about what a shipper can really pay while keeping the relationship intact; this stays with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: The person leads the conversation; AI only prepares and drafts around it.

in_practice.trigger: An account on the day's call list or an open dispute.
steps: Build a brief from AFAS history, mails and documents
Suggest payment-plan scenarios with cash effect
Officer calls and negotiates
Draft the confirmation mail for the officer to send
in_practice.human_gate: The officer leads the call; plans and extensions are approved by the officer or the Controller.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS debtor notes and plan records.

evidence.claim: Conversations, payment plans and extensions suit a copilot with the dispute file, with a person approving.

risks: Brief misses a recent promise made by sales
Officer leans on scripted offers instead of listening
Plan terms outside agreed limits
research_questions: How long does call preparation take today per account?
Are approval limits for plans and extensions written down?
Do briefed calls end in a firm promise more often in a trial?

tasks.short: Match Rabobank receipts to open invoices in AFAS and sort out the ones that don't match.

today.trigger: The daily Rabobank statement import into AFAS.
steps: Import the Rabobank statement into AFAS
Let AFAS auto-match what it can
Search mail for remittance details on unmatched payments
Post partial and combined payments by hand
Ask debtors about unclear payments
drudgery: Searching mail for remittance details
Splitting combined payments over invoices
today.time_sinks: Unmatched payments without a clear reference.

lenses.faster: AFAS rules match on reference, IBAN and amount; a model reads remittance mails for the rest and proposes the split; the officer checks only the proposals.
lenses.autonomous: Each statement import triggers matching; proposals above a confidence threshold post, the rest queue for the officer.
lenses.ambitious: Cash posted the same day, so the overdue list and credit holds are correct every morning: a decision made daily instead of after the weekly catch-up.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses hunting for remittance details; the officer wants more time on short payments that point to disputes.
lenses.altitude: The officer owns the matching rules and confidence thresholds and agrees them with the Controller and auditor.

tasks.human_edge: Working out what an odd or short payment means and calling the debtor about it.
tasks.pattern_why: AFAS rules do most matching; one model call reads remittance mails for the remainder.

steps: AFAS auto-matches on reference, IBAN, invoice number and amounts
Model reads remittance mails for unmatched lines
Propose matches and splits
Officer confirms low-confidence items and short payments
in_practice.human_gate: The officer approves matches below the confidence threshold and all short payments.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS bank journal with the match source noted.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches bank lines on payment reference, IBAN, invoice number and oldest-first sums; misses go to a person.
Genpact's AR suite expects up to 80% touchless cash application, as indicative estimates only.

risks: Wrong match clears the wrong invoice
Short payments hidden by automatic matching
Remittance details in unusual formats
research_questions: What share of receipts does AFAS match today without help?
Where do remittance details arrive, and in what formats?
What error rate will the Controller and auditor accept?

tasks.short: Keep debtor records clean: address and contact changes, merged or closed companies.

today.trigger: Returned mail, debtor notices or news of a KvK change.
steps: Receive a change notice by mail or returned post
Check the KvK register
Update the debtor in AFAS
Close or merge records of closed or merged companies
drudgery: Manual KvK lookups
Retyping address changes
today.time_sinks: Finding out a company closed or merged only after a reminder bounced.

lenses.faster: A scheduled KvK check compares debtor records and proposes updates; the officer confirms them in one batch.
lenses.autonomous: KvK changes trigger proposed updates that post for plain address changes; the officer handles closures and mergers.
lenses.ambitious: Weekly KvK status checks on every active debtor instead of finding out on a bounce: a decision made far more often.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping addresses; the officer wants more time on real risk cases.
lenses.altitude: The officer owns debtor data quality rules, including AVG retention for sole traders.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what happens to the open items of a closed, merged or insolvent company.
tasks.pattern_why: Comparing KvK data with AFAS records is a written rule.

in_practice.trigger: Weekly KvK check or a bounced mail.
steps: Compare AFAS debtor records with KvK data
Propose address and status updates
Officer confirms closures and mergers
Write updates to AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: The officer approves closures, mergers and any change touching open items.

evidence.claim: KvK lookups for monitoring and admin fit deterministic software at autonomy 4.

risks: KvK numbers missing in AFAS
AVG retention periods breached for sole-trader records
research_questions: How many debtors have a KvK number in AFAS?
What does a KvK change feed cost per year?

tasks.short: Hand unpaid accounts to the lawyer or collection agency, warn the credit insurer, block new orders.

today.trigger: No response after the final notice.
steps: Decide with the Controller to escalate
Collect invoices, reminders, contracts and correspondence
Send the file to the lawyer or agency
Notify the credit insurer and sales
Block new orders in AFAS
drudgery: Building the hand-over file
Recalculating interest and costs
today.time_sinks: Collecting a complete and correct file.

lenses.faster: An agent assembles the file with invoices, reminders, terms and interest calculation; the officer checks and sends it.
lenses.autonomous: Expiry of the final notice triggers a draft file and draft insurer notice; the officer and Controller decide.
lenses.ambitious: Earlier action on small debts that are now quietly written off, because a ready file makes escalation worth the cost.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses assembling files; the officer wants more say on when and how to escalate.
lenses.options: Comparing routes (agency, lawyer, settlement) with cost and expected recovery changes the decision itself.
lenses.altitude: The officer decides escalation routes within set limits and owns the checklist the lawyer relies on.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing whether legal steps are worth the cost and the customer relationship.
tasks.pattern_why: Files differ by case; a person decides before anything is sent.

in_practice.trigger: Final notice term expires without payment.
steps: Collect invoices, reminders, terms and mails
Calculate interest and costs by rule
Check the agency's Wki registration
Draft the hand-over file and insurer notice
in_practice.human_gate: The officer and Controller decide on escalation and approve the file before it is sent.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS debtor file and a SharePoint case folder.

evidence.claim: Syncasso turns a file into a draft summons in two minutes; handling time falls from 165 to 62 minutes, per the vendor.
Since 1 October 2026 no collection costs or further interest are owed if the party collecting on another's behalf is unregistered.
Early file errors surface only in court.

risks: Unregistered agency used, so costs are not recoverable from sole-trader debtors
Errors in the interest calculation
Order block hits a customer still in negotiation
research_questions: Are the agencies we use registered under the Wki?
How many files go to escalation per year?
Does the credit insurer accept digital notices?

role.altitude: From chasing invoices to running the order-to-cash rules: credit limits, reminder sequences, escalation routes, and dispute causes fed back to sales and operations.
reach: Bookkeeper (AR): cash application and dunning runs
Controller: credit limit proposals and small write-offs
role.ceiling_note: Negotiation and judgement on disputes, plans and escalation stay human, roughly 40% of the hours.
skills_to_grow: Writing and testing credit and dunning rules
Wki, BW 6:119a and AI Act basics
role.ambitious_version: A weekly cash-in forecast and a monthly dispute-cause report to sales and operations, so DSO is steered rather than explained.
